evals.name: react-toast-review
evals.expected_output: A markdown table reviewing the code with at minimum: framer-motion → motion/react migration, scale(0) → scale(0.95), ease-in → ease-out (or custom curve), transition: all → specific properties, duration too long. Should mention transitions over keyframes for rapidly-stacking toasts.

assertions.name: uses_review_table
assertions.check: Output contains a markdown table with Before, After, Why columns

assertions.name: flags_framer_motion_import
assertions.check: Output mentions migrating from framer-motion to motion/react (or motion package)

assertions.name: flags_scale_zero
assertions.check: Output flags initial/exit scale(0) and recommends scale(0.95) or similar non-zero starting scale

assertions.name: flags_ease_in
assertions.check: Output flags ease: 'easeIn' as wrong for UI and recommends ease-out or a custom curve

assertions.name: flags_transition_all
assertions.check: Output flags style.transition: 'all 500ms' and recommends specifying exact properties

assertions.name: flags_long_duration
assertions.check: Output flags 500ms duration as too long for a toast and recommends 200-320ms range

assertions.name: mentions_transitions_vs_keyframes
assertions.check: Output mentions that rapidly-stacking toasts benefit from CSS transitions over keyframes for interruptibility

evals.name: vue-drawer-build
evals.prompt: need a bottom sheet / drawer for my vue 3 app. should slide up from bottom on open, slide down on close, and let users swipe down to dismiss. using tailwind v4 and motion if i need it. what's the cleanest way to build this without going crazy with custom css?
evals.expected_output: A working Vue 3 + Tailwind v4 + motion-v drawer that uses theme easing tokens, swipe-to-dismiss with velocity threshold, prefers-reduced-motion handling, and momentum-based dismissal logic. Should NOT use framer-motion.

assertions.name: uses_tailwind_utilities
assertions.check: Output applies styles via Tailwind utility classes (transition-transform, duration-*, ease-*, translate-y-*) rather than hand-written CSS only

assertions.name: swipe_to_dismiss_with_velocity
assertions.check: Swipe-to-dismiss logic considers velocity, not just distance threshold

assertions.name: uses_translate_y_full
assertions.check: Drawer uses translate-y-full or translateY(100%) to hide off-bottom regardless of height

assertions.name: mentions_reduced_motion
assertions.check: Output addresses prefers-reduced-motion (motion-reduce: utility, useReducedMotion composable, or equivalent)

assertions.name: uses_custom_easing
assertions.check: Output uses a custom easing curve (ease-drawer / cubic-bezier 0.32 0.72 0 1) rather than just the default ease

evals.name: command-palette-decision
evals.prompt: quick question — i'm building a cmd+k command palette like raycast/linear. should the open/close have an animation? thinking like a 250ms fade+scale would feel polished. wdyt?
evals.expected_output: A clear recommendation against animating the open/close, citing how often users open the palette (100+ times/day), and pointing out that Raycast itself has no animation precisely because of this.

assertions.name: recommends_no_animation
assertions.check: Output clearly recommends NOT animating the open/close (or at most an extremely minimal one)

assertions.name: cites_frequency_reasoning
assertions.check: Output cites the frequency-of-use reasoning — keyboard-triggered, 100+ times/day, repeated daily use

assertions.name: mentions_raycast_or_keyboard_actions
assertions.check: Output references Raycast specifically OR the broader 'never animate keyboard-initiated actions' principle

assertions.name: no_blanket_yes
assertions.check: Output does NOT simply agree that 250ms fade+scale would be polished without challenging the premise
